prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using PROTACs and molecular glues to harness the ubiquitin-proteasome system.

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the most chemically original of the leading candidates. It replaces occupancy-driven inhibition with event-driven, catalytic induced proximity, so a small molecule can remove a protein instead of blocking it. Seven of eight members placed it in their top three, which shows unusual breadth of support across synthesis, biophysics, structural biology and medicine. The mechanism is well established: ternary-complex formation, E3 ligase recruitment and the cereblon explanation of thalidomide-class drugs. Independent groups have confirmed it for more than two decades, and many degraders are now in clinical trials. Crews and Deshaies founded the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept, and Handa's cereblon identification supplies the mechanistic basis of molecular glues. Together they cover both strands under one citation.
statement.case_against: No degrader has yet been approved, so clinical vindication is incomplete and the prize could be called early. Attribution is also genuinely crowded. Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito all have strong claims, and the three-name limit forces cuts that will be hard to defend whichever way they fall. The PROTAC and glue strands are separate lineages, and a single citation could be criticised as merging two discoveries to fit the limit.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B029 first but names Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, treating Ciulli's VHL-ligand work as what made PROTACs drug-like and leaving out the cereblon/glue strand (Handa, Ito).
responses.response: I take the Ciulli point seriously, since the VHL ligand and ternary-complex structures turned PROTACs from peptidic tools into drug-like molecules. But dropping Handa leaves the prize without the cereblon discovery, which explains thalidomide, lenalidomide and the whole glue field. That is a mechanistic discovery of the same weight as the PROTAC concept. I would keep Handa and accept that Ciulli is the third-place omission, which I regard as the weakest part of my configuration.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks B029 second behind Gray and Winkler's long-range electron transfer (B056), and proposes Crews, Ciulli and Handa while leaving out Deshaies. He judges the chemistry robust but the clinical side slightly early.
responses.response: I agree the mechanism is robust, and I take the clinical-maturity caution as a fair qualification. I disagree on Deshaies. The 2001 PROTAC paper was a joint Crews-Deshaies-Sakamoto effort, and the founding concept does not stand without both lead groups. On B056, I accept it is original and quantitatively rigorous, with decades of confirmation. But its impact beyond protein electron-transfer physics is narrower, and it shares the Marcus-theory lineage already recognised in 1992. I rank it below B029, though I would not oppose it as an alternative.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B043) first and B029 second. He notes that PROTACs and glues are separate lines that may have to be combined, and that recognition may be somewhat early.
responses.response: I agree the PROTAC and glue strands are distinct, which is why I credit both in one citation rather than pretend they are a single discovery. On timing, I do not think waiting for a first approval is required. The Nobel record shows that mechanistic confirmation and field-wide adoption matter more than a regulatory milestone. I respect B043's synthetic impact. But with 2010 already awarded for Pd cross-coupling, I see it as a refinement of a recognised area rather than a new modality.

responses.point: Aqvist places Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (B027) first, as a foundational and unambiguous theoretical-chemistry method with a clean two-person attribution.
responses.response: The two-person attribution and four decades of confirmation make B027 a clear scientific case, and I do not question its merit. My difference is one of priority. The chemistry community has recognised computational methods recently, and B027's ease of attribution does not make it more urgent than a new modality still being developed. I would be comfortable seeing B027 in a two-part prize alongside a biomedical topic, but as the sole award I would still place it second.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates (B055) first, as a generative physical-chemistry concept, but concedes that credit is crowded and that which cellular assemblies are truly phase-separated is still debated.
responses.response: This is the candidate closest to my own research on peptide self-assembly, so I am sympathetic to it. The same reasons you give hold me back: the physiological scope of phase separation is still disputed, and the credited group is broader than three. I would rather wait for the field to settle than reward a concept whose boundaries are being contested. B029's core mechanism is already settled.

uncertainties: Whether the third laureate should be Handa (cereblon, glues) or Ciulli (VHL, ternary-complex structure), and whether Sakamoto or Ito belongs in the configuration
Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug should delay recognition
Whether a two-part prize splitting PROTACs from glues would be fairer than one combined citation, given that the union is limited to three people
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My postdoc mentors (Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot. My field overlaps with Emma Sparr's on self-assembly, but this is not a personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate.
